In 2026, a pharmaceutical logistics firm is contracted to distribute temperature-sensitive vaccines across West and East Africa. Road quality, customs dwell times, electricity reliability, and last-mile arrangements with ministries of health differ sharply by corridor; some routes require passive cooling containers while others justify powered units; and seasonal weather windows constrain delivery schedules.

Design a cold-chain distribution strategy across African corridors with different infrastructure and institutional constraints, covering equipment choices, corridor sequencing, and contingency planning for spoilage risk.
